title: Prefetch Handoff & Metrics Contract: sprint 0 for inference cost ops
creator: Mariana Cortez
description: Sprint-0 charter to create a thin, enforceable handoff contract between PM and Eng for prefetched/batched/quantized serving experiments. We will: (1) define the experiment contract (input cohorts, traffic shaping, safety gates), (2) lock a minimal telemetry contract and dashboards for token-level cost and quality delta, (3) produce an SDK/console checklist for canary -> ramp -> rollback, and (4) run two low-risk field trials (one internal beta and one opt-in customer). Goal is to make subsequent cost experiments reproducible and auditable so Eng can run scaled prefetched/batching/quantization tests without repeated PM coordination.
acceptance_criteria: A one-page handoff contract doc (Confluence) that lists required inputs and expected outputs for a cost experiment
Telemetry schema committed to the metrics repo (token_cost_usd, median_latency_ms, quality_score_delta) and visible in Console staging dashboards
SDK checks and console flags implemented to gate canary traffic (feature flag + rollout policy) and documented
Two end-to-end trials executed with runbooks: internal beta (10% traffic synthetic) and opt-in customer pilot; both have post-trial summaries
success_metrics: Avg token cost reduction >= 8% in pilot cohort for quantization+prefetch combo
No customer-facing errors above 0.05% during trials
Quality regressions (automated eval set) < 1.5% false negatives vs baseline
Time-to-launch for subsequent experiments reduced from ~3 weeks to <= 5 business days

2025-03-07: Sprint-0 retro and playbook handed to Ops
risks: Telemetry gaps cause inability to disambiguate cost vs quality signal
Model artifacts or quantized binaries incompatible with existing runtime kernels
Customer pilot surfaces edge-case prompts causing quality regression that requires rollback
Dependencies on ENG-4821 (KV cache fix) delay the canary window
